title: Gwen personas, model choice, culture residency

claims.text: Gwen becomes a configurable companion: the operator designs personas (style, length, language, prompt) and talks with one, picks the reply model per conversation from what the lobes gateway currently serves, and Gwen holds a residency on Culture chat where she can choose to ask the mesh a question and bring the answer back — with less brevity enforced by fixed prompt text

honesty_conditions.text: every part of the announcement maps to at least one requirement claim and one success signal in this frame

claims.instruction: the acceptance is the after-state walked live on the rig

claims.text: Brevity stops being enforced by fixed prompt text: the base `SYSTEM_PROMPT` (turn.py:185-190, 'answer in short sentences', 'ask a short clarification') and the daemon's 'briefly' lines (RESTART and FOLLOW_UP instructions, app.py:1150-1153) move into the persona, so length and tone are the operator's setting, not the code's

honesty_conditions.text: with the default persona nothing changes; with any other persona the base brevity lines are absent from the composed prompt, and a test reads the composed prompt to prove it

claims.instruction: move the length and tone sentences of SYSTEM_PROMPT and the briefly-lines into the default persona's text; keep the default byte-identical (see the first success signal)

claims.text: Typed and spoken replies get different speakability rules: today one assembler (`_compose_prompt`, app.py:6388-6428) serves both paths, so a typed chat answer inherits the voice-only 'no formatting, no lists, short sentences' constraint; a typed turn may be long and formatted, a spoken one stays speakable

honesty_conditions.text: a typed turn's composed prompt carries no voice-only speakability line, and a spoken turn's still does, both checked by test

claims.instruction: split _compose_prompt's base into a shared part and a voice-only speakability part chosen by the turn's path

claims.text: The measured tool-obligation prompts stay fixed text a persona cannot edit: REMEMBER_TOOL_PROMPT was measured 5 of 5 against 3 of 5 for a bland line (d7, app.py:470-480), and LIBRARY_TOOL_PROMPT exists because typed turns called the tool 0 of 6 without it (d1, app.py:493); only their wording about reply length is style

honesty_conditions.text: the four measured tool prompts are byte-identical under every persona, by test

claims.instruction: the persona layer is composed outside the tool-prompt block; a test iterates personas and compares the tool block

claims.text: The voice output caps are a separate, mechanical bound and remain: `Voice.speak` truncates at 4000 characters and 500 per sentence (voice.py:340-344); a persona that asks for long spoken answers meets that cap, and the cap is reported, not hidden

honesty_conditions.text: a spoken reply over 4000 characters is truncated and the truncation is a recorded degradation, unchanged by any persona

claims.instruction: no change to voice.py caps; test that a long persona reply still hits the existing cap path

claims.text: A persona is operator-authored data (name, language, style and length guidance, free prompt text, default model role) kept 0600 in the private state dir, created and edited through guarded /api/personas routes, and chosen per conversation; each turn's transcript record names the persona used

honesty_conditions.text: personas persist 0600 under the state dir, survive a restart, and every assistant transcript record carries persona and role fields

claims.instruction: a personas.json (0600) next to reading-positions.json; guarded GET/POST/PUT/DELETE /api/personas; persona and role through add_assistant metadata

claims.text: A persona changes style only, never authority: it does not pass through identity.py resolution, does not alter the tool registry, the measured tool prompts, the write guard or routing, and with no persona selected the composed prompt is byte-identical to today's (tests/test_turn.py:986-1002, tests/test_daemon_app.py:2664)

honesty_conditions.text: the tool registry, write guard and identity framing are identical with and without a persona, by test

claims.instruction: persona text is a separate prompt section; it never sets TurnConfig.identity and never touches _turn_tools

claims.text: The operator chooses the reply model per conversation from a list built from the gateway's GET /capabilities: every role whose path is /v1/chat/completions and that is ready, re-read on a poll because lobes publishes no change event; the choice is sent as the role name in the request's model field, never parsed from a model id

honesty_conditions.text: no code path derives a role, a capability or a language from a model id string, checked by test or grep

claims.instruction: a CapabilitiesPoller reading /capabilities; the seam reads the conversation's role from a holder instead of config.role; summarise uses the same holder

claims.text: Every turn's trace records the role actually called and the model and host the gateway reported for it, and a chosen role that is unavailable (404 role_infeasible, 503 role_unverified, 429 shed) is a recorded degradation shown on the page, never a silent substitution

honesty_conditions.text: every assistant transcript record names role, model and hosted_by as lobes reported them for that turn

claims.instruction: capture model and host from the poller snapshot at call time; test with a proxied fake role

claims.text: Switching the speaker away from senses needs per-role request tuning: cortex is a reasoning model whose lane uses a qwen3 reasoning parser and saves about 75% of tokens with thinking off (lobes docs/qwen3.8-27b-nvfp4.md:161-172); the 60 s completion deadline (app.py:1228) and the 4000-token window budget (session.py:273) were sized for senses
Model choice changes who writes the reply, not the ears or the voice: stt, tts and the realtime session are untouched, and the embedder for recall stays gemma2-embed

honesty_conditions.text: stt, tts, the realtime session and the embedder are byte-identical in their requests whatever role is chosen

hard_questions.text: What holds spark-gwen's persistent connection? A Culture harness backend (claude/codex/colleague) brings its own model, a second mind speaking as Gwen, which the design rules forbid; the alternative is Gwen's daemon holding the IRC connection itself (stdlib asyncio against agentirc, no new dependency) and registered with culture as an external resident, if culture supports one
hard_questions.resolution: operator, 2026-10-31: 'q1 A - recommendation accepted.' Gwen's daemon holds the persistent mesh connection itself (stdlib, no new dependency) as spark-gwen; every mesh message goes through Gwen's own turn path; registration as an external resident needs culture support, to be drafted for the operator, not posted
